articleTitle: High T/sub c/ superconductors applied to generators, transformers and fault current limiters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: High temperature superconductors (HTS) offer potential technical and economic advantages compared to conventional conductors and low temperature superconductors. In this paper salient points are highlighted concerning the following power devices operating with HTS components at 77 K: a.c. synchronous generators, generator power transformers and fault current limiters. Of the devices considered, the most likely near term and commercially attractive is the superconducting fault current limiter (SCFCL). In particular, the electrical properties required for an inductive shielded type of SCFCL operating at 77 K are achievable with HTS material available today.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: The discovery of high temperature superconductivity has re-awakened interest in the transmission of energy using force cryocooled superconducting cables as a method of reducing the cost of electric power transmission. The area of impact for the new superconductors is in the supertension area of high power underground cables. Within defined operating parameters, superconducting cables offer an economic alternative to conventional underground cables in certain circumstances and in some cases offer unique solutions to systems planners. One major impact could be in future environmental demands and the energy savings possible with appropriate designs of cable are attractive.

abstract: The author reviews the development of high T/sub c/ superconductors. The preparation techniques of the ceramic materials and the applications of materials for power devices are discussed.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Superconducting magnets have been available for about three decades and are used for a variety of applications notably in the research laboratory. High temperature superconductors (HTS) open up the prospect of magnets for very high fields at temperatures easily accessed. This article considers the practical aspects of such HTS magnets.

articleTitle: Thick film applications of high temperature superconductors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: High temperature superconductors (HTS) are described with particular reference to three promising applications. The first is the use of HTS thick film resonators in coupled cavity resonators for use as filters at 0.9 and 1.8 GHz. The second is the combination of superconductors and dielectric resonators to provide high Q devices for frequency standards and filters. The third is the use of HTS in the receiver coils used in magnetic resonance imaging machines where a key goal is enhanced signal to noise.

articleTitle: Precursor powders for the fabrication of high temperature superconductor ceramics for practical applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Precursor powders play an important part in the progress of HTSC ceramics towards commercial realisation. Many powder related issues must be resolved before precursors ideal for the formation of optimal cuprate ceramics can be achieved. There is evidence that all powder issues can be addressed and resolved by use of spray pyrolysis as the fundamental method of powder production. We will continue to follow this approach to develop improved precursor powders for the manufacture of HTSC ceramics for practical applications.

articleTitle: Local power distribution using high T/sub c/ superconductors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Over the past seven years considerable advancement has been made to produce high temperature superconductor materials in suitable forms for power application. The performance of the materials is constantly being improved and it is foreseen that the basic elements for superconducting machinery, cables and transformers will be available in due course. The requirements of critical current density and field dependence of such are greater for some applications than others and, because of this, it is likely that the superconducting fault current limiter (SC-FCL) will be an early application. It is also increasingly realised that for other superconducting equipment to be successfully utilised on the power network will require a SC-FCL.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of High Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Ceramic superconductors experience losses when carrying alternating currents. A practical situation of particular importance for the possible use of such superconductors in power apparatus is 50 Hz excitation at liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K). A theoretical investigation of the one-dimensional AC current flow and associated losses in a ribbon or tape of YBCO, the cross-section of which is assumed to be much wider than its thickness, is considered in this paper.
